passages.text: and the combination of the two farfield values should yield a freestream turbulent viscosity between 10^-5 and 10^-2 times freestream laminar viscosity.
passages.why: The far-field k and omega together should give an eddy viscosity of 1e-5 to 1e-2 times the laminar one; the studio's SST ratio of 1 is far above that range and is not taken from this page.

passages.heading: "Standard" Menter SST Two-Equation Model (SST) and (SSTm)
passages.text:
The boundary conditions recommended in the original reference are:

$$\frac{U_{\infty}{L} < \omega_{\rm farfield} < 10 \frac{U_{\infty}{L}$$

$$\frac{10^{-5}U_{\infty}^2}{Re_L} < k_{\rm farfield} < \frac{0.1 U_{\infty}^2}{Re_L}$$
passages.why: The recommended far-field ranges of the SST model: omega between U/L and 10 U/L, and k between 1e-5 and 0.1 times U^2 / Re_L, with L the length of the domain.

passages.heading: "Standard" Menter SST Two-Equation Model (SST) and (SSTm)
passages.text: Thus, the farfield turbulence boundary conditions are somewhat open to interpretation. Note that the turbulence variables decay (sometimes dramatically) from their set values in the farfield for external aerodynamic problems.
passages.why: What is set at the far field is not what reaches the airfoil: k and omega decay on the way in, so the far-field numbers are a loose choice.

passages.heading: Menter SST Two-Equation Model with Controlled Decay (SST-sust) and (SST-sust-m)
passages.text: corresponds to a freestream Tu level of 0.08165%.
passages.why: For the controlled-decay variant, which the studio does not use, the recommended far-field k is a turbulence intensity of about 0.08%, the same order as the studio's 0.1%.

passages.heading: Menter SST Two-Equation Model with Controlled Decay (SST-sust) and (SST-sust-m)
passages.text: The reason is that these values have been adjusted to allow a drastic decay before the fluid approaches the body.
passages.why: The usual far-field k and omega of the standard model are chosen with the decay before the body in mind.
